sentences.text:
THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER Heard Sri. Chandrashekar P.V., learned counsel appearing for petitioners; Sri. Prathap S.S., learned counsel on behalf of NC: 2024:KHC:50288 WP NO.27576 OF 2023 Sri. Monesh Kumar K.B.,
learned counsel appearing for the respondent.
2.

The relevant facts for adjudication of this writ petition are that the schedule properties have been acquired by the respondent-Authority for the purpose of widening of existing Hosur-Bengaluru Road between Central Silk Board to Junction up to Yenky Factory.

In this regard acquisition proceedings has been initiated in respect of various properties including the schedule properties and accordinlgy, respondent-Authority had passed award on 06th December, 2015 and determined the market value of the acquired property at Rs.2,278/- per Sq. Ft.

The petitioners have received the award notice and have filed application under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short,
hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') for enhancement of market value before the City Civil Court,
Sri. Narayanaswamy.

3 Bengaluru, which ought to have been filed before the Respondent-Authority.

sentences.text:
The applications filed by the petitioners have been registered as Miscellaneous Nos.723/2015, 220/2016, 221/2016,
222/2016 and 219/2016.

Thereafter, petitioners have filed memo seeking withdrawal of the aforementioned cases and NC: 2024:KHC:50288 WP NO.27576 OF 2023 accordingly, the reference Court had dismissed the same on 06th April, 2021 at the instance of the petitioners.

3. It is also stated in the petition that the respondent- Authority had acquired the properties of other claimants along with the properties of the petitioners and some of the owners of the properties,
being dissatisfied with the quantum of market value awarded by the respondent-Authority, have made an application under Section 18(1) of the LA Act for determination of higher market value.

Accordingly, the respondent-Authority had referred the said applications to the II Additional City Civil Judge, Bengaluru for determination of higher market value and same was registered as L.A.C.
No.38/2016 and connected cases.

entities.text: II Additional City Civil Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Reference Court, after considering the material on record,
had enhanced the market value at Rs.6,930/- per Sq. Ft. as against Rs.2,278/- Per Sq. Ft.
determined by the respondent-Authority.

It is also stated in the petition that the petitioners have filed application, seeking re-determination of compensation under Section 28-A of the LA Act read with Section 73 of the new Land Acquisition Act, 2013 before the respondent-Authority in terms of the award made by the Reference Court in L.A.C. No.38/2016 and connected cases.

NC: 2024:KHC:50288 WP NO.27576 OF 2023 Thereafter, the petitioners, being aggrieved by the inaction of the respondent-Authority in not considering the applications filed by the petitioners under Section 28-A of the LA Act, have filed Writ Petition No.9797 of 2022 and Writ Petition No.24421 of 2022 before this Court, seeking direction to the respondent- Authority to consider their applications for re-determination of the market value as per award made by the Reference Court in LAC No.38/2016 and connected cases.

This Court, by order dated 19th May, 2022 in Writ Petition No.9797 of 2022 and order dated 07th December, 2022 in Writ Petition No.24421 of 2022, disposed of the petitions with a direction to the respondent-Authority to consider the case of petitioners in accordance with law.

In terms of the order passed by this Court in the above writ petitions, the respondent-Authority, after considering the applications made by the petitioners, had issued Endorsements dated 09th August, 2023 (Annexure-C) and 20th June, 2023 (Annexure-D) stating that, Miscellaneous First Appeal No.6323 of 2023 is pending consideration before this Court and ordered for awaiting the judgment that may be passed by this Court in the above said Miscellaneous First Appeal.

Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of Annexure-E series would indicate that, this Court in Miscellaneous First Appeal No.6321 of 2021 and similar other appeals had observed that the respondent- Authority shall deposit 50% of the award amount before the Reference Court and petitioner/claimants are at liberty to withdraw the same.

Accordingly, this Court in the present writ petition also, by order dated 13th March, 2024, had directed the respondent-Authority to deposit 50% of the enhanced market value along with all statutory benefits,
before this Court.
Sri. Narayanaswamy.

In this regard, learned counsel appearing for petitioners has filed memo dated 02nd December,
2024 for disbursal of amount in deposit in terms of direction issued by this Court on 13th March,
2024.

The said memo reads as under:
"MEMO FOR DISBURSAL OF AMOUNT IN DEPOSIT The petitioner submit

that,
pursuant to the deposit made by the Respondent, the petitioner have an application for withdrawal of compensation amount in deposit.

The petitioners submit that,
petitioners 2 to 5 are the Joint owners and so also petitioners 6 to 8 also.
Therefore the Respondent NC: 2024:KHC:50288 WP NO.27576 OF 2023 has deposited the compensation without bifurcating their respective shares.
The aforesaid petitioners have only individual Bank S/B Accounts and it is also difficult to the registry to transfer the amounts in the joint names by way of RTGS/K2 Challan.

Under the circumstances, to avoid complications and to meet the ends of justice it is just and necessary to direct the registry to disburse the compensation in the following manner in the interest of justice and equity.
